QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_36

question.text: Sahyadri Impact Fund has committed capital of INR 1,000 crore and has called INR 800 crore from LPs. Compute the PIC Multiple.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.4.1: PIC Multiple = Paid-in Capital / Capital Commitments = 800 / 1000 = 0.80 or 80%. A high PIC means the fund is near end of its drawdown phase — with INR 200 cr dry powder remaining. The Trap: 0.20 is the 'uncalled %'. 1.25 inverts the ratio. 1.00 is the full-commitment case. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test the PIC multiple. Cambridge and Preqin report PIC alongside DPI/RVPI/TVPI. Manager's Pro-Tip: Report PIC every quarter — LPs use PIC with RVPI to estimate 'remaining mark-up potential': low PIC + high RVPI = late-stage fund positioned for further distributions; high PIC + low RVPI = early fund still deploying.
